best_for: Neovim users who want a desktop window with smooth scrolling, ligatures and a cursor that is easy to follow, without changing their config.

points.title: A window for the Neovim you already have
points.text: Neovide is a GUI only. You need Neovim 0.12 or later installed separately, and your plugins and init.lua work as they do in the terminal.

points.title: Motion you can follow
points.text: The cursor smears as it moves, with optional particle effects, scrolling is smooth to the pixel, and windows glide into place. Floating windows get a blurred background.

points.title: Fonts render properly
points.text: Ligatures, font shaping and emoji fallback work, which some terminals struggle with.

points.title: Remote and WSL
points.text: `--wsl` opens a window for Neovim running in WSL, and `--server` attaches to a Neovim that is already running over TCP, a socket or a named pipe.

points.title: A spare-time project
points.text: The maintainers say it is built in spare time, so fixes depend on volunteers. It is MIT-licensed and free.

points.title: Versions kept here
points.text: Windows installs machine-wide, x64 only, and the Windows listing keeps 19 versions. Mac has Intel and Apple Silicon builds for macOS 12 or later. The Flathub build, at 0.17.2, is not marked verified by Flathub. Mac and Linux list only the current release.
